candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Egyptian state museums lend objects rarely seen outside Cairo; Hong Kong's positioning as neutral cultural broker made this happen.

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: The Met exports adornment traditions across cultures; test of Hong Kong's luxury-adjacent audiences beyond European painting.

candidates.title: Wonders of Imperial Carpets: Masterpieces from the Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
candidates.blurb: Islamic textile masterworks from Doha; Hong Kong leveraging Gulf museum networks in ways Western capitals cannot.

candidates.title: A Movable Feast: The Culture of Food and Drink in China
candidates.blurb: Palace Museum material culture of dining; serious scholarship on a topic Hong Kong actually lives daily.

candidates.title: The Forbidden City and The Palace of Versailles: China-France Cultural Encounters in the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
candidates.blurb: Jesuit exchange objects and court chinoiserie; Hong Kong as platform for parity narratives between empires.

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Major private textile collection surfaces publicly; rare window into Hong Kong collector culture beyond bronzes and scroll paintings.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: Repatriation of Hong Kong's Venice Biennale collateral pavilion; indicator of what curators think plays internationally versus locally.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: Permanent Hong Kong art survey; measure of how the official canon has shifted in recent institution rebuilds.

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Export porcelain and Canton trade painting; reclaiming the middleman aesthetic as a Hong Kong inheritance.

candidates.title: Tai Kwun Neon Connection
candidates.blurb: Long-term neon installation in heritage compound; low-key preservation of sign-making craft amid rapid erasure citywide.

candidates.title: On Ink and Bamboo: The Hua-e Jiaohui Lou Donation
candidates.blurb: Private scholar-painting collection enters public trust; signal of generational wealth handover in traditional collecting circles.

candidates.title: Heavenly Horses: Masterpieces from the Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Equestrian iconography across dynasties; Beijing lends top-tier works for prolonged runs unavailable to Western institutions.
